decisions.reason: The product shows clear customer cost savings and remained visible through 2024, so its performance likely exceeds aspiration levels and the firm has enough growth and innovation slack to continue it.
As a close-to-core machine with its own page in both 2023 and 2024, it appears at least satisfactory relative to aspirations, and the firm's expansion reduces pressure to withdraw it quickly.

The 2024 website cites both large annual savings and a named customer investment case, which strongly suggests performance above aspiration and little reason for problemistic search away from the product.
This 2024 launch is very close to the established shredding business, and although evidence is still limited, the firm's current growth and R&D strength give it slack to keep testing and selling it.

Because it is newer and somewhat more exploratory than the core range, its results are more uncertain, but the growing firm and industry make continued retention more likely than a near-term withdrawal.
